Palette SDK is the SiMa.ai software development toolkit for building AI
applications on Modalix. It includes the development environment, runtime
library, model tooling, and DevKit validation workflow. Together, these
components support the full development path: prepare a model, build an
application, and validate the result on Modalix hardware.

Use this overview to understand the main parts of Palette SDK and choose the
right setup, model preparation, or application development path.

![Palette SDK software stack showing the development environment, Neat Library, Model Compiler, LLiMa, and Modalix DevKit](https://developer.sima.ai/software/assets/images/neat-software-stack-animated-6a51bd7a41fcf3d5f058e1d4f6e3e4b7.svg)

Developer journey

If you are new to Palette SDK

There are two supported ways to develop applications with Palette SDK:

- **[Use the Palette SDK](https://developer.sima.ai/software/getting-started/dev-environment/)** when you want a more performant development environment,
especially if you plan to compile models, or cross-compile large scale C++ code.
- **[Develop directly on the DevKit](https://developer.sima.ai/software/getting-started/neat-library/)** when you want fewer moving parts with the development environment, especially when you are not doing model compilation work.

If you choose the SDK path, confirm your host meets the
[host requirements](https://developer.sima.ai/software/getting-started/dev-environment/#host-requirements), then
install the SDK. SDK installation applies compatible defaults, so you only need
the Compatibility reference when you want to pin exact versions, upgrade
components independently, or troubleshoot a version mismatch.

**SDK-only fast path (no DevKit):** install the SDK, then go straight to
[Compile a Model](https://developer.sima.ai/software/compile-a-model/). Configure SDK, DevKit Sync, the Neat
Library, and PyNeat are optional side-trips you can skip until you pair a DevKit.

Reading the commands

Command blocks in the setup and application guides are labelled and
colour-coded with the environment they run in, so you never have to guess where
to type them:

| Prompt | Run it |
| --- | --- |
| `host$` | On your own machine, outside the SDK. |
| `sdk$` | Inside the Palette SDK container shell. |
| `devkit$` | On the Modalix DevKit. |
| `pcie-host$` | On the host machine holding the Modalix PCIe card. |

A block labelled with more than one environment, such as `sdk or devkit$`, runs
the same way in either place.

## Start Here

Prepare your host machine, Palette SDK, and DevKit for local development and hardware validation.

- [**Palette SDK** Use the SDK for a high performance host-based workflow, model compilation, C++ builds, and DevKit validation.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/getting-started/dev-environment/)
- [**Neat Library** Install runtime and PyNeat directly when you want fewer moving parts to prototype apps on a DevKit.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/getting-started/neat-library/)
- [**Compatibility Guide** Reference guide for supported version combinations.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/getting-started/compatibility/)

## Model Preparation

Turn trained models into deployable artifacts that run on Modalix hardware.

- [**Compile a Model** Compile pretrained ONNX vision models or GenAI models for Modalix.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/compile-a-model/)
- [**Use a Precompiled Model** Start quickly with a ready-to-run model artifact.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tools/model-zoo/)
- [**GenAI with LLiMa** Compile, test, and benchmark GenAI models on Modalix.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/genai-llima/)

## Build an App

Use the Neat Library to run models and compose production application pipelines.

- [**Hello Neat!** Run your first Neat application and verify the development workflow.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/hello-neat/minimal/)
- [**Develop Apps** Build AI applications with the Neat Library using C++ or PyNeat.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/)
- [**Tutorials** Follow guided examples for real Neat application patterns.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tutorials/)
